text:
Ana Chen: Quick update — starting next billing cycle (2026-06-01) we’re enabling a soft quota buffer for hosted API customers. This is a rate-tolerance layer that prevents transient spikes from immediately triggering overage invoices. Read below for details. :eyes:

Devon Patel: TL;DR: buffer = 5% of monthly committed tokens up to 1M tokens. It will be applied automatically; we’ll surface a dedicated line item on the invoice called `soft_quota_buffer` so customers see when it was used. No extra charge for the buffer itself — customers only pay for tokens consumed beyond quota+buffer.

Mike Rosario: From infra side: routing and rate-limiters will now use a three-tier check: 1) token bucket (per-key), 2) soft-buffer allowance, 3) hard quota enforcement. If soft buffer triggers, requests are still served but flagged for analytics and invoicing. Example config snippet:
```
rate_limit: 100rps
soft_buffer_pct: 5
soft_buffer_max: 1000000
```

Devon Patel: We also cleaned up invoice line items: `usage_tokens`, `soft_quota_buffer`, and `overage_charges`. This should reduce support tickets asking "what is this cost?" — and we’ll include mapping to API keys and routes in billing exports.

Ana Chen: No change to free-tier allocation. Free credits will not be impacted by the buffer. If a customer hits hard quota (after buffer) they will be throttled as before.

billing-bot: Invoice preview for account acme-inc updated: https://billing.redwood.ai/invoices/preview/ACME-2026-06 - generated 1823456840

Mike Rosario: Ops note — we’ll roll the soft buffer to hosted gradually over two weeks starting 2026-05-15; Dedicated customers can opt in via their account rep. Private deployments are unaffected unless customers enable the same setting locally.

Jordan Kline: Appreciate the clarity — please add a short blurb for the public docs (announcements page + changelog). :tada:

Ana Chen: On it. We'll post a public blog + changelog entry the morning of the rollout. If anyone spots wording that might cause support volume, flag me directly.
